prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a mortgage application waiting on payslips. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When payslips are missing because a member has only just been paid, it is usually best to pause the case briefly rather than chase repeatedly; a net pay line up with the application and bank statements before moving the case on."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a member says they are paid weekly or four-weekly, I prefer to ask for the presented."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a payslip looks cropped, blurred or incomplete, I prefer to ask for a fresh copy straight away rather than trying to interpret partial figures and risking a rework later."},{"type":"fact","content":"When bank statements show salary arriving on a different day from the payslip date, that is not necessarily a problem, but the employer name and
